title: Per-minute session credit framework - brief
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:

This brief specifies the Per-minute Session Credit Framework (PM-SCF) — a standardized metering and contract abstraction that converts session-duration and fidelity demands into a compact credit unit for pricing, entitlements, and SLO reconciliation. The goal is to make session-based commercial agreements tractable for both developers and commercial teams while preserving predictable economics under bursty, multimodal conversational workloads.

Intended audience:
- Product managers and pricing leads
- Solutions and sales engineers
- Billing & revenue operations
- Runtime and telemetry engineers

Goals and success metrics:
- Provide a single canonical credit unit ("session-minute credit") that maps to runtime cost signals (GPU-time, token throughput, KV cache pressure).
- Enable per-customer contracts that are: auditable (billing events traceable to telemetry), predictable (<=10% monthly variance against the projected spend for typical workloads), and fair (credits align with resource cost).
- Reduce complexity of commercial negotiations by supporting 3 contract primitives: baseline monthly commit, burst buffer credits, and fidelity-adaptive discounts.

Definitions and primitives:
1) Session-minute credit (SMC): the atomic billing unit. One SMC represents the cost-equivalent of a single minute of median conversational throughput for a defined fidelity profile. The SMC is not a time measurement in the runtime; it is a cost-normalized token-time abstraction.
2) Fidelity profile: a label defining resource intensity (e.g., "low-emb", "conv-standard", "conv-high-fidelity"). Each profile has a conversion multiplier to SMCs.
3) Baseline commit: monthly SMC allocation included in the contract at discounted unit pricing.
4) Burst credits: pool of pre-purchased on-demand SMCs at a higher unit cost for transient peaks.
5) True-up: monthly reconciliation comparing actual SMC consumption to baseline commit.

Conversion and calibration model (high level):
- SMC conversion is derived from a workload-weighted runtime cost model using three telemetry signals: average active GPU-seconds per session-minute, average tokens emitted per session-minute, and observed KV cache hit ratio.
- Formula (conceptual):
  SMC = alpha * GPU_seconds_per_minute + beta * tokens_per_minute * token_cost_index - gamma * cache_hit_saving
- Alpha/beta/gamma are tuned quarterly by the pricing analytics team and published as a conversion table.

Pricing tiers and rate sheet (example table):
- Baseline SMC unit price (example): Standard fidelity: $0.020/SMC; High fidelity: $0.045/SMC; Embedding-heavy sessions: $0.012/SMC
- Burst SMC price multiplier: 2.0x baseline unit price
- Minimum monthly commit: 50,000 SMCs (can be negotiated)

Contract clauses (example YAML snippet for legal and billing coders):
  contract_component: "baseline"
  currency: "USD"
  baseline_commit_smc: "50000"
  unit_price_usd_per_smc: "0.02"
  burst_buffer_smc: "10000"
  burst_unit_price_multiplier: "2.0"
  true_up_window: "monthly"

(Embed this snippet into the standard commercial template. It will be converted into billing line items by RevOps.)

Telemetry and enforcement:
- Required telemetry events (minimum): session.start, session.heartbeat (1m cadence), session.end, model.variant, fidelity_profile, session.kv_hit_rate, tokens.emitted.
- Billing will consume the session.heartbeat stream to compute per-session SMCs; implementations MUST ensure heartbeats are emitted at the configured cadence to avoid undercount/overcount disputes.
- Telemetry contract examples:
  - session.heartbeat payload should include: session_id, timestamp, active_gpu_seconds, tokens_emitted, fidelity_profile, kv_hit_ratio.

SLO and reconciliation workflow:
1) Realtime: the runtime exposes a per-route SMC burn-rate gauge to the Console (1m resolution) and alerts when burn-rate deviates ±25% from expected based on the selected fidelity profile.
2) Monthly true-up: RevOps computes actual SMC consumption by aggregating heartbeats and applying the published conversion table; invoices reflect baseline used, burst usage, and any negotiated credits.
3) Dispute process: customer disputes must include raw heartbeat exports for the disputed month. The standardized CSV export format is described in Appendix A. Disputes window: 60 days after invoice issuance.

Operational playbook for onboarding a customer to PM-SCF (numbered rollout steps):
1. Pre-sales sizing: Solutions engineer runs the Session Simulator with the customer’s workload sample to estimate median tokens/min and expected fidelity mix; produces a projected SMC consumption report.
2. Contracting: Pricing selects baseline tier and rate, RevOps adds burst buffer and sets SLA credits for underperformance.
3. Instrumentation: Runtime team enables heartbeat stream and verifies event schema.
4. Pilot (30 days): Customer runs production traffic with a capped burst buffer. Telemetry is monitored daily and an initial reconciliation is produced at day 30.
5. Finalize commit: Based on pilot results, either adjust the baseline commit or migrate customer to a consumption-only pricing plan.

Migration and edge cases:
- Legacy customers on per-token metering can be migrated by running a 60-day shadow conversion and presenting a migration credit that amortizes risk over 3 billing cycles.
- For long-duration streaming sessions (multihour), we cap per-session SMC at 6x per-hour baseline to avoid runaway invoices. Exceptions must be approved by RevOps.
- Offline batch embedding jobs should default to an embeddings fidelity profile; if runtime is run on Dedicated, conversion should use Dedicated-aware multipliers.

Telemetry schema (Appendix A) (CSV export columns):
- invoice_period, customer_id, session_id, heartbeat_timestamp, active_gpu_seconds, tokens_emitted, fidelity_profile, kv_hit_ratio, derived_smc

Rollout plan and timeline (recommended):
- Q4 2026: finalize conversion table, implement heartbeat consumer in Billing pipeline, internal pilot with 3 strategic customers.
- Q1 2027: public launch for new customers (opt-in for legacy customers).
- Q2 2027: telemetry-driven optimizations and quarterly update of alpha/beta/gamma coefficients.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Inaccurate heartbeats lead to billing disputes. Mitigation: require SDK and runtime validation tests and sample export for first bill cycle.
- Risk: High-fidelity burst patterns create unpredictable cost for the vendor. Mitigation: conservative burst pricing and optional soft caps with automated throttles.

Ownership and decision rights:
- Product (owner): finalize fidelity profile taxonomy and conversion policy.
- Pricing & RevOps (owner): rate sheet, contract templates, true-up process.
- Runtime & Telemetry (owner): heartbeat implementation, Console burn-rate gauges, export tooling.
- Legal (owner): contract language and dispute clauses.

Appendix B: Example customer scenario (worked example):
- Customer A: median conversational session 2.5 tokens/sec, average session length 6 minutes, fidelity mix 70% conv-standard, 30% conv-high-fidelity.
- Apply conversion table -> estimated SMC/month = 75,000. Pricing team proposes baseline commit 70k SMC @ $0.02 -> monthly baseline $1,400; burst buffer 10k SMC @ 2.0x -> on-demand buffer.

Action items (next steps):
- Product to publish v1 conversion table (owner: Maya) by 2026-12-15.
- Runtime to deliver heartbeat consumer and example CSV exporter by 2027-01-05.
- RevOps to draft contract clause templates and invoice mapping by 2027-01-20.
